question: An ascitic fluid SAAG of 0.8 g/dL (serum albumin 3.5 g/dL, ascitic albumin 2.7 g/dL) indicates that portal hypertension is the likely cause of the ascites.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. SAAG = serum albumin (3.5) − ascitic albumin (2.7) = 0.8 g/dL, which is below the 1.1 g/dL threshold. A SAAG <1.1 g/dL rules out portal hypertension as the cause of ascites and points to non-portal-hypertensive aetiologies.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A SAAG of 0.8 g/dL is below the threshold of 1.1 g/dL. Values <1.1 g/dL indicate that ascites is NOT due to portal hypertension; consider malignant ascites, tuberculous peritonitis, pancreatitis, or nephrotic syndrome.
